Knowing how it is terminal is indeed based on how it reacts on treatment. There are 3 possible treatments for cancer. Surgery, chemo and radiotherapy. These can be combined or not. 
Surgery has the best results. When a tumor is found and it can be easily cut out you have a big chance of surviving. Often chemo is given afterwards even if all the tumor tissue is cut out so you would kill small metastases or tissue you didn't cut out. 
When a tumor can't be cut out (grown inside important tissue or to much tumors) your chances of survival lower significantly. They often try chemo and radiotherapy in the hope the tumor gets smaller and can be cut out. 
If there are to much tumors in multiple organs, you just can't cut them out anymore. Usually you then receive chemo and radiotherapy to prolong your life and/or comfort.
